Monday • Upper Body Pull Workout

Pull-focused upper-body session covering back, biceps and core. All exercise photos are embedded locally so the page works without external image loading.

Final Equipment Version

  • No resistance band.
  • No seated cable row → Chest-supported dumbbell row.
  • No back-extension machine → Bodyweight bird dog.
  • Bird dog stays bodyweight because your Friday lower-body session already includes RDLs.

1. Pre-workout

  • Hydrate before training.
  • Normal meal 1.5–3 hours before, or a light snack 30–60 minutes before if needed.
  • Use loads leaving about 1–2 good reps in reserve.
  • Stop for sharp pain, dizziness, chest discomfort or unusual symptoms.

2. Warm-up • 10–12 min

5 min treadmill / cross trainer
Easy → moderate pace. The goal is to raise body temperature, not fatigue yourself.

Wall Slides

10 reps

Focus: Shoulder mobility and scapular control

How to perform
  1. Stand with your back against the wall.
  2. Keep your ribs down and move your arms slowly upward.
  3. Use a comfortable range.
  4. Do not force your hands or elbows against the wall.
Open original reference

Scapular Push-ups

2 × 10

Focus: Serratus and shoulder-blade activation

How to perform
  1. Start in a high plank, or use knees-down.
  2. Keep elbows straight.
  3. Let the chest sink slightly as the shoulder blades come together.
  4. Push the floor away and spread the shoulder blades.

Warm-up visual check: 5 movement references are included below: Arm Circles, Shoulder-Blade Squeezes, Wall Slides, Scapular Push-ups and Light Lat Pulldown.

Warm-up order: 5 min cardio → arm circles 15 forward + 15 backward → shoulder-blade squeezes 2×15 → wall slides 10 → scapular push-ups 2×10 → light lat pulldown 1×15.

4. WOD • Research Pictures + Instructions

Lat Pulldown

2 × 10–12 • Rest 60–90 sec

Focus: Lats, upper back and biceps

How to perform
  1. Set the thigh pad firmly against your thighs.
  2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
  3. Sit tall with a small, comfortable lean.
  4. Drive your elbows down toward your ribs.
  5. Bring the bar toward the upper chest.
  6. Return the bar slowly until the arms are extended.
Do not pull behind the neck or use a large swinging motion.
Open original reference

Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row

2 × 10–12 • Rest 60–90 sec

Focus: Lats, rhomboids, traps and rear delts

How to perform
  1. Set the bench around 30–45 degrees.
  2. Place your chest firmly on the pad and feet on the floor.
  3. Let the dumbbells hang below your shoulders.
  4. Pull your elbows back and slightly toward your hips.
  5. Pause briefly near the top without shrugging.
  6. Lower under control to a full comfortable stretch.
Keep your chest on the bench. Do not lift your torso to move the weight.
Open original reference

Bird Dog

2 × 8–10/side • Rest 45–60 sec

Focus: Core and spinal stability

How to perform
  1. Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
  2. Brace your abdomen gently.
  3. Extend the opposite arm and leg.
  4. Keep hips level and spine neutral.
  5. Hold 2–3 seconds.
  6. Return slowly and alternate sides.
Keep this bodyweight for now. Your Friday plan already includes RDLs.
Open original reference

Dumbbell Curl

1 × 10 • Rest 45 sec

Focus: Biceps

How to perform
  1. Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides and palms facing forward.
  2. Keep upper arms close to your torso.
  3. Curl by bending the elbows.
  4. Squeeze near the top.
  5. Lower slowly to full comfortable extension.
Open original reference

5. Cardio Finish

Stationary bike • 10 min • RPE 5–6/10

2 min easy → 6 min steady moderate → 2 min gradually easier.

6. Cool-down • 8–10 min

Doorway Chest Stretch

30 sec/side

Focus: Chest and front shoulder

How to perform
  1. Place your forearm against a doorway.
  2. Step forward gently.
  3. Rotate your torso away until you feel a mild chest stretch.
  4. Keep the shoulder relaxed.
  5. Do not bounce.
The exact doorway-chest photo from the earlier search was hosted on a site that blocked direct download, so it is intentionally not used here.
Open original reference

Cross-body Shoulder Stretch

30 sec/side

Focus: Rear shoulder

How to perform
  1. Bring one arm across your chest.
  2. Use the opposite hand to gently draw it closer.
  3. Keep the stretching shoulder relaxed.
  4. Hold for 30 seconds and switch sides.
The visual is a clear shoulder-mobility reference. Follow the written cross-body instructions.
Open original reference

Overhead Triceps Stretch

30 sec/side

Focus: Triceps

How to perform
  1. Raise one arm overhead.
  2. Bend the elbow so the hand moves behind the head.
  3. Gently guide the elbow downward.
  4. Keep your torso upright and avoid forcing the shoulder.
Open original reference

Upper Trap / Neck Stretch

30 sec/side

Focus: Upper trapezius and neck

How to perform
  1. Relax the shoulder on the stretching side.
  2. Gently tilt your head toward the opposite side.
  3. Use only light hand assistance if needed.
  4. Hold without pulling hard.
Open original reference

Child's Pose

45–60 sec

Focus: Back, lats and shoulders

How to perform
  1. Kneel on the floor.
  2. Sit your hips toward your heels as comfortable.
  3. Reach your arms forward.
  4. Relax your shoulders and breathe slowly.

7. Post-workout

  • Rehydrate.
  • Have a protein-rich meal within the next few hours.
  • Include carbohydrates if the session was demanding.
  • Record weights and reps.
  • Prioritize sleep and recovery.

Gym-floor Cheat Sheet

Warm-up: 5 min cardio → arm circles 15/15 → shoulder squeezes 2×15 → wall slides 10 → scapular push-ups 2×10 → light pulldown 1×15.

WOD: Pulldown 2×10–12 → chest-supported row 2×10–12 → bird dog 2×8–10/side → curl 1×10.

Finish: Bike 10 min → chest stretch → cross-body shoulder → triceps → neck → child's pose.

All exercise photos in the main WOD are embedded locally. The “Open original reference” buttons are optional source links.

Scheduling Guidance

Recommended split: Perform the Pull and Push workouts about 2–3 days apart. A simple template is Monday Pull → Wednesday Push → Friday Lower Body. This spacing gives roughly 48 hours of recovery for the same muscle groups before training them again.

Why 2–3 days? Upper-body muscles generally need 48–72 hours to recover from a hard strength session. Spacing the sessions by 2–3 days keeps weekly volume high without overloading any single movement pattern.

If you can only train twice per week: Pair Pull + Lower Body on one day and Push + Lower Body on the other, or alternate Pull/Push every 3–4 days.
